transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm doing this right, I've never really... well, I just don't want you to think badly of me or think I'm crazy, because I'm usually really good at my job and very put together. 

But... what brought me in is, um, I keep hearing this man’s voice. It comes from the garage vents at the shop, and sometimes right from under the hood when I'm working on a vehicle. It’s as clear as somebody standing right next to me, handing me a wrench. And he just... he keeps telling me not to trust my husband, or he tells me not to touch certain cars. 

I'm sorry, I know how strange that sounds to say out loud. Is that... is that the kind of thing you needed to know?
How long have you been hearing this man's voice — was it just the past day or two, a few weeks, or has it been going on for months?

Um... well, it's definitely been longer than a few weeks. I... I really hope you don't think less of me, because I've still been doing a really good job at the shop, I promise. But... it's actually been going on for about ten months now. 

And, um... I guess I should just tell you everything so I'm doing this right. For those same ten months, along with the voices, I've also been having these... these thoughts that I'm being tracked. Like people are keeping tabs on me or following what I do. 

I'm so sorry, I know how paranoid and crazy that sounds. I really try not to let it bother me. Am I giving you too much information, or is that helpful for you to know?
Have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications around the time these voices and tracking feelings started?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. I don't... I don't really drink much at all, maybe a glass of wine at a wedding or something, but that's it. And I've never touched any kind of drugs. I know some people in my line of work do, but I take my job very seriously, and I would never want to do anything to jeopardize that or make myself unreliable. 

And as for medications, no, I haven't started anything new. I just take a regular multivitamin. I really try to take good care of myself. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I know it doesn't explain why this is happening to me, but... I just wanted you to know I'm not doing anything to cause it on purpose. Is that... is that what you were hoping to hear?

Over these past ten months, have you noticed any changes in how you're managing daily responsibilities—work, relationships, or self-care—like difficulty concentrating, withdrawing from people, or needing to change your routine because of these experiences?

Um... well... I guess things have changed a little bit. But I really try my best to keep everything normal, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything. 

At work, um... well, the voice tells me not to touch certain cars, right? So I guess I might have hesitated a few times, and... well, I made a couple of small mistakes. My boss is really nice, though, and they just... they pulled me off the high-voltage EV work for a little while. Just because they were worried about safety, which makes total sense! I agreed with them, it was the responsible thing to do. 

And at home... well, my husband and I usually get along great, but... things have been a little tense. We've been arguing more than usual, mostly because I'm so worried about being tracked and I guess it's hard for him to understand. It got a little loud the other night, and... well, he actually ended up taking me in for an emergency evaluation. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds really bad. I really am trying to hold it all together. I hope you don't think I'm a terrible employee or a bad wife... am I doing okay explaining this?
Besides the voice and feeling tracked, have you noticed any changes in how you speak or organize your thoughts, or has anyone commented that your behavior seems unusual or hard to follow?

Um... no, no, I don't think so. I really try to be clear when I talk to people, especially at the shop. I mean, nobody has said anything to me about... about me not making sense or anything like that. 

I guess... well, sometimes when I'm really worried about the tracking, I might get a little flustered, but I always make sure to pull myself together. I don't want to be a burden or confuse anyone, you know? I try really hard to keep my thoughts organized so I can do my job right and be a good partner to my husband. 

Does that... does that sound normal to you? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

Have you noticed any changes in your emotions or motivation lately—like feeling less interested in things you used to enjoy, having a harder time showing emotion, or wanting to withdraw from people even when you're not worried about being tracked?

Well... I mean, I guess there have been some days where I'm just... not quite myself. But I really try not to let it affect anyone else! I don't want to be a downer, you know? 

It's just... sometimes, I've had these stretches where I don't call anyone back. And I've been skipping the church potlucks, which I feel terrible about because I used to help run them and people rely on me for that. But lately, I'll just sit in the house, or sometimes even in the bay at work, just... staring at my tools. It's like I can't even make myself care about any of it, even though I know I should. 

I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't be slacking off like that. I really am trying to push through it and be more involved again. I don't want to seem lazy or ungrateful for the things I have. Is it okay that I feel that way sometimes? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I've given up.

Do these periods of low motivation and pulling away from people happen only when the voices or tracking fears are especially strong, or do they also occur as a separate stretch of feeling down or low in energy even when you're not preoccupied with those experiences?

Um... I'm actually not entirely sure? I hope it's okay to say I don't really know for sure. I try so hard to just keep a positive attitude, so I haven't really kept track of the exact timing of it all. 

I guess... it feels like it mostly just happens when the worries are really heavy. Like, when I'm so stressed out about the tracking or when the voice is being really strict with me, it just takes all my energy. And I think that's when I kind of shut down and just sit there staring at my tools, because I'm just so worn out from trying to hold it all together. I don't think I really have times where I'm just feeling low for absolutely no reason... at least, I haven't noticed that happening. 

I'm so sorry, I wish I could give you a clearer answer! Am I still being helpful? I really want to make sure I'm doing a good job explaining things for you.
Over these past ten months, has there ever been a period of at least a couple of weeks where you did NOT hear the voice or feel tracked at all?

Um... no, no, not really. I mean, I wish I could say yes, because I know it would probably sound better, but... no. 

For the whole ten months, it's pretty much been there the whole time. The voice and the tracking, I mean. I try really hard to ignore it and just put on a brave face, especially for my husband and the guys at the shop, but it hasn't really gone away for even a week, let alone a couple of weeks. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not what you wanted to hear. I really am trying my best to handle it, though! I haven't missed a day of work because of it, I promise. Is... is it really bad that it's been going on that long without a break? I hope you don't think I'm not trying hard enough to get better.
{"intent": "Rule out an underlying medical/neurological cause for the psychosis (e.g., head injury, seizures, thyroid or other illness) that would point away from a primary

Um... no, no medical stuff like that. I mean, I try to take really good care of myself! I eat right and I don't get sick very often at all. 

I definitely haven't hit my head or had any seizures or anything scary like that. And I had a physical for work a while back, and they said my thyroid and everything was totally fine. I'm actually really healthy, physically speaking! 

I hope that's okay? I know sometimes it's easier if there's just a simple medical reason for things, so I'm sorry if this makes it more complicated for you to figure out. I promise I'm completely healthy otherwise, though!
Has anyone—like your husband or coworkers—noticed you doing anything unusual with your body, like unusual postures, freezing in place, or repetitive movements, during these past ten months?

Um... no, definitely not. I mean, I hope they haven't noticed anything like that! I try really, really hard to act completely normal around everyone. 

I don't think I do any of those things, like freezing up or moving weirdly. I mean, sometimes if I'm really stressed about the tracking, I might just sit quietly at my workbench for a minute to collect myself, but I always make sure I look like I'm just focusing on a part or taking a quick break. My husband hasn't said anything, and the guys at the shop haven't either. I really pride myself on keeping up appearances and not letting anyone see me struggle. 

Is... is it okay that I don't have any of those symptoms? I hope I'm not missing anything important that you need to know. I really am trying to be as helpful and accurate as possible for you!

Um... I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch what you just said. Could you repeat that for me? I just want to make sure I answer correctly and give you exactly what you're looking for. Am I doing okay so far?

Have you or anyone close to you noticed that your facial expressions or emotional reactions seem flatter or less animated than they used to be, even when something happens that would normally make you smile or show emotion?

Um... well, I really try to be friendly and upbeat, especially at work. I don't want anyone to think I'm rude or anything! But... I guess there are times lately where I just... I don't know, I just kind of check out? 

Like, there are stretches where I just don't call anyone back. And I used to help run the church potlucks—I always made sure I was there early to set up—but lately, I've just been skipping them. It's not that I don't like the people, I just... I can't seem to muster up the energy to care. Sometimes I'll just sit in the house, or even in my bay at the shop, just staring at my tools. It's like I can't make myself care about any of it, even things I usually like. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound awful or lazy. I really do try to keep a smile on my face when people are talking to me. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it right.
